existing.description: The Friedrich-Ebert-Stiftung's basic funding programme for international students supports Bachelor's, Master's, Diplom and Staatsexamen degree programmes at German public or state-recognised universities. The published financial support is 992 Euro, with health insurance costs covered and an additional 255 Euro per month for scholarship holders with children. The scholarship does not have to be repaid and is awarded independently of need.
eligibility: You are already studying at a German public or state-recognised university or university of applied sciences
You have very good German language skills
You have above-average grades in your studies
You are socially and politically engaged
You identify with the values of Social Democracy
The programme covers Bachelor's, Master's and Diplom degree programmes as well as programmes leading to the Staatsexamen
existing.eligibility_summary: International students at a German public or state-recognised university with very good German, above-average grades, social-political engagement and identification with the values of Social Democracy.
benefits: Extensive programme of socio-political seminars, workshops and skills training
18 thematic working groups and local scholarship-holder groups in many cities
Integration into the network of current and former scholarship holders
Personal support and advice from former scholarship holders
The scholarship does not have to be repaid
coverage: Additional 255 Euro per month for scholarship holders with children
requirements: Applications have to be submitted in German
Applications are submitted online via the FES online application form
First graded transcripts (erste benotete Leistungsnachweise) are a prerequisite for applying
application_method: Complete the online application form for the study scholarship
Submit the supporting documents and expert opinion (Unterlagen und Gutachten)
existing.selection_notes: The selection procedure has five steps (online application form, documents and expert opinion, first selection interview, second selection interview, decision by the selection committee). From application to decision it can take three to seven months. Applicants who are the first in their family to study and/or have a migration background, as well as women and students at universities of applied sciences and in STEM subjects, are considered in particular.
existing.best_fit: International students who are already enrolled at, or applying to, a German public or state-recognised university for a Bachelor's or Master's degree and who have very good German and above-average grades.
existing.notes: Applications are formally possible both from Germany and from abroad. Good German is required even if the degree programme is taught in English; the foundation states that it accepts level B2 even without a certificate. The FES does not fund second degrees, part-time or dual studies (except where full-time study is evidenced), short-term stays abroad, internships, summer schools, language courses or final-exam-only phases.
existing.application_period: Rolling within the published degree-stage windows; for Master's programmes starting in the winter semester, applications are due by 30 November.
existing.deadline_display: Master: before or at the start of the first university semester of the master's programme (winter semester: by 30.11.; summer semester: by 31.05.). Bachelor / Diplom / Magister / Staatsexamen: after the first semester and up to three semesters before the end of the standard period of study.

existing.description: The Konrad-Adenauer-Stiftung's refugee scholarship programme funds Bachelor's, Master's and PhD students who hold a German residence permit. The page is published bilingually in English and Ukrainian. For undergraduate and graduate students the financial support is up to 752 Euro per month depending on income plus 300 Euro for study-related expenses; for PhD candidates it is 1,350 Euro per month plus 100 Euro for research-related expenses. Applications are made online via campus.kas.de.
eligibility: You have completed your schooling and studies with above-average grades
You identify with the political stances represented by the Konrad Adenauer Foundation
You are involved in voluntary work in political, social and cultural areas
You are willing to actively participate in the scholarship programme
You are interested in a broad range of topics beyond your research area and appreciate exchange in a multicultural environment
As a refugee in Germany you are entitled under specific legal requirements to study and to apply for a scholarship

existing.eligibility_summary: Students in Germany with a refugee-related residence permit, above-average academic achievements, identification with the values of the Konrad-Adenauer-Stiftung, voluntary engagement and initiative.
benefits: For PhD candidates: encounters with personalities from the public sector and intensive exchange through the KAS network of over 17,000 alumni
coverage: Financial support for undergraduate and graduate students of up to 752 Euro per month depending on your income or the income of your parents, plus 300 Euro for study-related expenses such as books and writing material
Financial support for PhD candidates of 1,350 Euro per month plus 100 Euro for research-related expenses, with further allowances possible
Wide range of seminars on political, economic, academic and cultural topics
Access to an extended network of scholarship holders and alumni
Career counselling and support with the first steps into the labour market
Individual support and consultations in all matters regarding the PhD and scholarship by KAS staff and special academic advisors at the university
requirements: Upload all required application documents as part of the online application
documents: Written-out and tabular curriculum vitae of up to three pages (undergraduate and graduate students)
Certified copy of the admission letter from your German university
Letter of assessment of your academic skills (e.g. by a professor at your university)
Copy of the transcript of your university grades and courses (or single course certificates)
Copy of all your academic diploma and training certificates
Proof of German language skills at B2 level (undergraduate and graduate students)
Proof of advanced German language skills (at least equivalent to Goethe-Zertifikat C1); a language certificate is required (PhD candidates)
Application form with your professional and personal development and your social and/or political engagement (PhD candidates)
Written-out, signed and dated curriculum vitae of 4,000-6,000 characters including spaces, plus a signed and dated tabular CV (PhD candidates)

Two letters of assessment of your academic skills by your supervisor and another university professor, both entitled to supervise a doctoral thesis and not older than six months before the application deadline, submitted by the applicant (PhD candidates)

Proposal of your PhD project of five to ten pages with literature appendix, covering topical actuality and social or political relevance, the main problems and solution approaches, research design and methods, and a tentative timeframe (PhD candidates)
application_method: Confirm your residence permit qualifies you for the relevant programme route
Prepare the document set for your degree stage (undergraduate/graduate or PhD)
Upload all documents before the round closes on 15 January or 15 July
existing.selection_notes: Selection criteria are open-mindedness, high commitment and a wide range of interests, above-average academic achievements, social engagement and willingness to assume social and political responsibility, and identification with the foundation's values and views. PhD applicants must have a doctoral supervisor who is familiar with and supports the proposal.

existing.notes: The page states the foundation supports undergraduate (Bachelor), graduate (Master) and postgraduate (PhD) students, with different financial and non-financial services per scholarship type. A Ukrainian translation of the same information is published on the same page.
existing.application_period: Two annual rounds: applications close on 15 January and 15 July each year; the next round after 2026-10-01 closes on 15 January 2027.
existing.deadline_display: Apply online on campus.kas.de until 15 January or 15 July annually.
